#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# Vanguard Ballistics: Android App Bundle (.aab) Build Script
# Uses Google's official Bubblewrap CLI (Trusted Web Activity - TWA)
# Produces Google Play Store ready App Bundle: app-release-bundle.aab
# ==============================================================================

set -e

echo "=== VANGUARD BALLISTICS: ANDROID APP BUNDLE GENERATOR ==="
echo "Target Package: com.vanguard.ballistics"
echo "Format: Android App Bundle (.aab)"

# 1. Check if Node.js is installed
if ! command -v node &> /dev/null; then
    echo "Error: Node.js is required to run Bubblewrap."
    exit 1
fi

# 2. Check if Java is installed (needed for Android SDK compiler)
if ! command -v java &> /dev/null; then
    echo "Notice: Java (JDK 17+) is required by Gradle to compile .aab on this machine."
    echo "If building locally or in CI/CD (GitHub Actions), ensure openjdk-17-jdk is installed:"
    echo "  sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y openjdk-17-jdk"
fi

# 3. Check for existing twa-manifest.json
if [ ! -f "twa-manifest.json" ]; then
    echo "Error: twa-manifest.json not found in project root."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Step 1: Installing / invoking @bubblewrap/cli..."
# Run bubblewrap build using the existing twa-manifest.json
npx @bubblewrap/cli build

echo ""
echo "=== BUILD COMPLETE ==="
echo "Your production Android App Bundle has been compiled to:"
echo "  ./app-release-bundle.aab"
echo ""
echo "Next Steps for Google Play Console:"
echo "1. Log into Google Play Console (https://play.google.com/console)"
echo "2. Create or select 'Vanguard Ballistics'"
echo "3. Go to Release > Production / Internal Testing"
echo "4. Upload 'app-release-bundle.aab'"

# Vanguard Ballistics: Android App Bundle (.AAB) Project

This is the complete, official Trusted Web Activity (TWA) Android project for Vanguard Ballistics: Tactical Operations.

## How to Build the Android App Bundle (.aab):

### Option 1: Using Android Studio (Recommended)
1. Open Android Studio.
2. Select **Open** and choose this `android-project` folder.
3. Wait for Gradle sync to complete.
4. Click on the top menu: **Build > Generate Signed Bundle / APK...**
5. Select **Android App Bundle** (.aab) and click Next.
6. Create or select your release keystore.
7. Click **Create** / **Finish**.
8. Your `.aab` file will be generated in `app/release/app-release.aab` ready for Google Play Console!

### Option 2: Using Command Line (Terminal)
```bash
# In this directory:
./gradlew bundleRelease
```
The compiled Android App Bundle will be output to:
`app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab`

### Option 3: Google Play Console Upload
1. Log into https://play.google.com/console
2. Select your app: **Vanguard Ballistics** (`com.vanguard.ballistics`)
3. Navigate to **Release > Production** (or Internal Testing)
4. Upload `app-release.aab`
5. Roll out to Google Play!

=== .github/workflows/opencode.yml
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}"
on:
  issues:
    types:
      - opened
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Existing issue to run
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    outputs:
      approved: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.approved }}
      issue_number: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);
              appendFileSync(env.GITHUB_ENV, `OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN=${token}\n`);
              break;
            } catch (error) {
              if (attempt === 7) throw error;
              await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, Math.min(20000, 3000 * 2 ** attempt)));
            }
          }
          NODE
      - name: Register preparation
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 2 --retry-all-errors --max-time 15 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{\"run\":\"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\",\"attempt\":$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT,\"sequence\":1,\"state\":\"starting\",\"phase\":\"initializing\"}" \
            "$OMGITHUB_ORIGIN/api/github/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER/run"
      - name: Checkout trusted preparation code
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Validate and claim issue request
        id: prepare
        env:
          OPENCODE_ACCESS: ${{ vars.OPENCODE_ACCESS || 'writers' }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: /usr/bin/time -p node .omgithub/scripts/opencode-prepare.mjs
      - name: Report branch handoff
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.redispatched == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          sequence=$(/usr/bin/time -p node -p 'Date.now()')
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 2 --retry-all-errors --max-time 15 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{\"run\":\"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\",\"attempt\":$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT,\"sequence\":$sequence,\"state\":\"starting\",\"phase\":\"queued\"}" \
            "$OMGITHUB_ORIGIN/api/github/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER/run"
      - name: Report preparation failure
        if: ${{ always() && (failure() || cancelled()) }}
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ job.status }}
        run: |
          sequence=$(/usr/bin/time -p node -p 'Date.now()')
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 2 --retry-all-errors --max-time 15 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{\"run\":\"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\",\"attempt\":$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT,\"sequence\":$sequence,\"state\":\"ended\",\"phase\":\"initializing\",\"outcome\":\"$OUTCOME\",\"reason\":\"Workflow preparation failed. Check build details.\"}" \
            "$OMGITHUB_ORIGIN/api/github/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER/run"
      - name: Keep two newest runners
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: /usr/bin/time -p node .omgithub/scripts/run-slots.mjs
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    concurrency:
      group: omgithub-runner-admission-${{ github.repository }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    timeout-minutes: 5
  opencode:
    runs-on: ${{ contains(needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json, '"mac"') && 'macos-latest' || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    timeout-minutes: 305
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
      pull-requests: write
    env:
      SSH_NAME: opencode-issue-${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}-${{ github.run_id }}-ssh
      OPENCODE_WEB_PORT: 4096
      PROJECT_PATH: ${{ vars.PROJECT_DIR || './' }}
      PROJECT_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ vars.PROJECT_DIR || './' }}
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL: "true"
      OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKSPACES: "true"
      OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA: "true"
      OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_MODELS: "true"
      OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS: "true"
      OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WEBSOCKETS: "true"
      TARGET_OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
      TARGET_REPO: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}
      TARGET_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      TARGET_REF: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      TARGET_SHA: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
      RUNTIME_REF: ${{ github.workflow_sha }}
      APP_PORT: 3000
      BRANCH_NAME: opencode/${{ github.run_id }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY != '' }}
      TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
      COMMENT_BODY: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      LABELS_JSON: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      TEST_REQUEST: ${{ contains(needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json, '"test"') && contains(needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json, '"OpenCode"') }}
      GOAL_REQUEST: ${{ contains(needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json, '"Goal"') }}
      RALPH_REQUEST: ${{ contains(needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json, '"ralph"') }}
      OMO_REQUEST: ${{ contains(needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json, '"omo"') }}
      SSH_ONLY_REQUEST: ${{ contains(needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json, '"ssh"') }}
      VALIDATION_ENABLED: ${{ vars.VALIDATION_ENABLED || 'true' }}
    steps:
      - name: Record job start time
        shell: bash
        run: echo "JOB_STARTED_AT=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);

content.text:
Good: static HTML project supported. We need to create index.html, styles, JS game. Need to include Android bundle files from attachment into repo (so the build request is honored). Probably place them at android/ or root as provided. The attached bundle contains TWA config and android project. We'll copy into repo e.g. `android/` plus maybe root twa-manifest? The user says "Build" with attachment. Likely they want the game and the android bundle applied. I'll integrate the Android/TWA files into the repo (under `android/` maybe at root? The zip has top-level android-project, icons, scripts, twa-manifest.json, well-known). I'll copy contents to root so they're preserved, and add game files. But careful: scripts/build-android-bundle.sh at root is fine. The default start script ignores those.

Game concept: "Vanguard Ballistics: Tactical Operations" — landscape tactical top-down shooter. Need complete playable game with ballistics (bullet drop? ricochet? penetration?), tactical operations, gunsmith armory, campaign mode per manifest shortcuts. Should be polished and mobile-friendly.

Let me plan the game design deeply to make it fun and complete:

Genre: Top-down tactical shooter with realistic ballistics, cover, enemy AI, squad? Player controls a vanguard operator in procedurally generated/level-based missions. Aim with mouse/touch, shoot with trigger; movement WASD/left joystick. Weapons have recoil, spread, bullet velocity/travel time, penetration, ricochet, magazine/reload, grenades, dash. Enemies with vision cones, cover, patrol, alert states. Objectives: eliminate hostiles, secure intel, reach extraction. Campaign of ~6 operations with escalating difficulty. Gunsmith: unlock/upgrade weapons with credits. Persistence localStorage.

Given time constraints, aim for a single-file-ish or modular JS app with canvas 2D rendering, no dependencies. Must look great. Need screenshots via playwright.

Core features:
- Menu / mission select / armory / settings / how-to-play.
- Top-down 2.5D-ish visuals: dark tactical palette, grid floor, walls, crates, cover, fog of war/vision cones, muzzle flashes, tracers, bullet casings, blood/sparks, screen shake, lighting vignette, scanline, HUD.
- Player: health, armor, stamina/sprint, ammo, grenades, dash/roll maybe. Reload. Weapon switching between primary and sidearm.
- Aiming: mouse aim, click/hold fire; touch: dual sticks (left move, right aim/fire). Auto-fire when aim stick engaged, or dedicated fire button. Landscape orientation.
- Ballistics: projectiles with speed, drag, penetration through cover depending on material and weapon penetration; ricochet chance; bullet drop? Top-down, could simulate velocity and damage falloff; wall penetration with damage reduction. Bullet trails. Tracer.
- Enemy AI: patrol, investigate gunfire, take cover, flank, shoot bursts with telegraph (laser aim), grenades later. Different types: grunt, marksman (laser), heavy (shield), drone? Keep 3 types.
- Levels: tile-based map with walls, crates, sandbags, explosive barrels, extraction zone, intel. Multiple missions with handcrafted maps via procedural generation seeded.
- Objectives: eliminate all hostiles + reach extraction; some missions "recover intel" then extract. Timer? Credits reward based on accuracy, time, health.
- Campaign progression with mission unlock, difficulty.
- Gunsmith armory: buy weapons (SMG, rifle, shotgun, DMR, LMG), attachments/upgrades (scope, extended mag, suppressor, armor-piercing) with credits. Equip primary/secondary.
- Audio: WebAudio synthesized gunshots, ricochets, explosions, UI clicks, ambient. Mute toggle.
- Settings: audio, screen shake, aim assist? touch sensitivity.
- Pause menu, mission complete/failed screens, restart.
- Tutorial/help overlay.
- Save in localStorage.

Rendering: canvas at devicePixelRatio capped, fixed world camera follow with slight lookahead toward aim, zoom adaptive. Use offscreen canvas for static level? Simple draw.

We need robust collision: circle vs axis-aligned rectangles (walls, crates). Line of sight raycast vs rects. Bullets step with substeps and collide with rects (penetration: reduce damage/velocity per material, ricochet if angle shallow and material hard). Bullet vs actors circle collision along segment.

Maps: build from a grid string maybe 48x32 tiles with '#' walls, 'C' crates, 'S' sandbag (low cover? but top-down cover blocking LOS and bullets), 'B' barrel explosive, '.' floor. Spawn points. Use 32px tiles, world 1536x1024. Camera zoom ~0.9 on desktop.

Need mobile landscape, but also portrait phones? Manifest orientation landscape. We can show rotate prompt in portrait for phones? Better support portrait too? Tactical top-down with dual sticks works portrait; but request implies landscape. We'll design responsive: if portrait on phone, show "rotate device" overlay (and allow tap to continue?) Simpler: allow play in both, adapt camera. But safe: show rotate hint non-blocking. I'll support both, with HUD scaled. The game should fill viewport.

Implementation structure:
- index.html (menu DOM overlays, canvas)
- css/style.css
- js/audio.js, js/input.js, js/world.js? Might be simpler to modularize: main.js with all? Large file maybe 2500+ lines. Modular is cleaner: 
  - js/util.js (math, rng, storage)
  - js/audio.js
  - js/content.js (weapons, missions, upgrades)
  - js/entities.js (player, enemy, bullets, particles)
  - js/maps.js (level gen)
  - js/game.js (state, update, render)
  - js/ui.js (menus, HUD DOM)
  - js/main.js (bootstrap)
Need no build step; use ES modules. Static server default works.

Testing: playwright-cli. Need to serve with start.sh? Use tmux persistent server per Agents.md. Could use `python3 -m http.server 3000` or the default start (node default-start). Simpler: python http.server in tmux. But capture.sh expects port? The runtime default likely serves on APP_PORT=3000. We can use start.sh in tmux which runs node default-start; it watches. Let's do `tmux new -d -s serve 'bash start.sh'`. Then playwright-cli open http://localhost:3000 (or 3002? Agents.md mentions 3002 for Pascal). APP_PORT 3000. default-start probably uses 3000. Check default-start quickly.

Also the Android bundle: include assetlinks with host? Existing assetlinks probably generic. We'll copy all bundle files into repo root; but "well-known/assetlinks.json" should be `.well-known/assetlinks.json`. The zip uses "well-known" without dot perhaps because hidden. I'll preserve and maybe rename to `.well-known`. Also need PWA manifest and service worker for TWA to work. The TWA manifest references manifest.webmanifest and pwa icons at root. We can create manifest.webmanifest, pwa icons (copy from bundle icons), sw.js, and place icons at root. That makes the web app installable/TWA-compatible, aligning with bundle. Also `.well-known/assetlinks.json` with placeholder fingerprint from bundle. Good touch.

Let me look at assetlinks and icon, colors.

export function upgradeSet(save) {
  return new Set(save.upgrades || []);
}

export function playerMods(save) {
  const up = upgradeSet(save);
  return {
    maxArmor: up.has('armor') ? 140 : 100,
    speed: up.has('boots') ? 1.1 : 1,
    grenades: up.has('pouch') ? 5 : 3,
    focusCooldown: up.has('focus') ? 13 : 19,
    suppressed: up.has('suppressor'),
    armorPlates: up.has('armor'),
  };
}

export function resolveWeapon(id, save) {
  const base = WEAPONS[id] || WEAPONS.vector;
  const up = upgradeSet(save);
  const w = { ...base };
  if (up.has('ap')) {
    w.dmg = base.dmg * 1.08;
    w.pen = base.pen + 1;
  }
  if (up.has('optic')) w.spread = base.spread * 0.82;
  if (up.has('mag')) w.mag = Math.round(base.mag * 1.5);
  if (up.has('suppressor')) {
    w.suppressed = true;
    w.sound = 'suppressed';
  }
  w.reserve = Math.round(base.reserve * (up.has('mag') ? 1.25 : 1));
  return w;
}

export function threatDots(level) {
  return '◆'.repeat(level) + '◇'.repeat(Math.max(0, 6 - level));
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down tactical shooter based on the provided Vanguard Ballistics Android bundle.

## Requirements
- Build the game now, without clarifying questions.
- Complete, playable scope with reasonable assumptions.
- The build should support desktop and mobile layouts.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for own visual checks, reading only the latest.

## Decisions
- Assumed the provided bundle is source/reference material and built it as a browser-playable PWA with a six-operation campaign.
- Implemented synthesized audio rather than external audio assets.
- Copied Android bundle artifacts into the existing repository under `android/`.

export function upgradeSet(save) {
  return new Set(save.upgrades || []);
}

export function playerMods(save) {
  const up = upgradeSet(save);
  return {
    maxArmor: up.has('armor') ? 140 : 100,
    speed: up.has('boots') ? 1.1 : 1,
    grenades: up.has('pouch') ? 5 : 3,
    focusCooldown: up.has('focus') ? 13 : 19,
    suppressed: up.has('suppressor'),
    armorPlates: up.has('armor'),
  };
}

export function resolveWeapon(id, save) {
  const base = WEAPONS[id] || WEAPONS.vector;
  const up = upgradeSet(save);
  const w = { ...base };
  if (up.has('ap')) {
    w.dmg = base.dmg * 1.08;
    w.pen = base.pen + 1;
  }
  if (up.has('optic')) w.spread = base.spread * 0.82;
  if (up.has('mag')) w.mag = Math.round(base.mag * 1.5);
  if (up.has('suppressor')) {
    w.suppressed = true;
    w.sound = 'suppressed';
  }
  w.reserve = Math.round(base.reserve * (up.has('mag') ? 1.25 : 1));
  return w;
}

export function threatDots(level) {
  return '◆'.repeat(level) + '◇'.repeat(Math.max(0, 6 - level));
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# Vanguard Ballistics: Android App Bundle (.aab) Build Script
# Uses Google's official Bubblewrap CLI (Trusted Web Activity - TWA)
# Produces Google Play Store ready App Bundle: app-release-bundle.aab
# ==============================================================================

set -e

echo "=== VANGUARD BALLISTICS: ANDROID APP BUNDLE GENERATOR ==="
echo "Target Package: com.vanguard.ballistics"
echo "Format: Android App Bundle (.aab)"

# 1. Check if Node.js is installed
if ! command -v node &> /dev/null; then
    echo "Error: Node.js is required to run Bubblewrap."
    exit 1
fi

# 2. Check if Java is installed (needed for Android SDK compiler)
if ! command -v java &> /dev/null; then
    echo "Notice: Java (JDK 17+) is required by Gradle to compile .aab on this machine."
    echo "If building locally or in CI/CD (GitHub Actions), ensure openjdk-17-jdk is installed:"
    echo "  sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y openjdk-17-jdk"
fi

# 3. Check for existing twa-manifest.json
if [ ! -f "twa-manifest.json" ]; then
    echo "Error: twa-manifest.json not found in project root."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Step 1: Installing / invoking @bubblewrap/cli..."
# Run bubblewrap build using the existing twa-manifest.json
npx @bubblewrap/cli build

echo ""
echo "=== BUILD COMPLETE ==="
echo "Your production Android App Bundle has been compiled to:"
echo "  ./app-release-bundle.aab"
echo ""
echo "Next Steps for Google Play Console:"
echo "1. Log into Google Play Console (https://play.google.com/console)"
echo "2. Create or select 'Vanguard Ballistics'"
echo "3. Go to Release > Production / Internal Testing"
echo "4. Upload 'app-release-bundle.aab'"
echo "5. Submit for review and publish!"

## Objective
- Finish and verify the existing browser-playable Vanguard Ballistics game, including its campaign, skirmish mode, and PWA/Android packaging.

## Requirements
- Provide a six-operation campaign and endless skirmish mode.
- Support desktop, mobile, touch, and gamepad layouts.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for visual checks and read only the latest.

## Decisions
- Continue from the existing implementation and validate it in-browser rather than restarting.
- Use synthesized audio and procedural maps; retain Android packaging artifacts under `android/`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `js/main.js`, `manifest.webmanifest`, and `sw.js`.
- Ran desktop browser checks covering menu, deployment, combat, pause, campaign results/progression, armory, settings, and skirmish waves/retry; no runtime errors were observed.
- Ran mobile touch checks for twin-stick movement/aim, pause, and portrait rotation hint.
- Improved touch HUD visibility, mobile landscape menu layout, enemy contrast, lighting, and touch camera framing.
- Saved visual-check JPEGs under `/tmp/opencode/shot-*.jpg`; latest checks include mobile and desktop gameplay screenshots.

### Active
- Finish the visual/runtime pass and review the latest edits for regressions.
- Verify PWA assets and Android configuration against the completed web app.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Re-run desktop and mobile checks after the latest CSS/renderer changes; inspect only the newest screenshots.
2. Check remaining gameplay flows and controls, including reloads, weapon switching, upgrades, loading, exfil, and gamepad input.
3. Validate `manifest.webmanifest`, service-worker cache entries, and Android TWA host/asset association; fix mismatches or missing assets.
4. Review `git status` and summarize the uncommitted changes and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: application initialization and module wiring.
- `js/game.js`: simulation, combat, mission flow, and persistence.
- `js/render.js`: canvas renderer, lighting, camera, and visual effects.
- `js/ui.js`: menus, HUD, panels, and results.
- `css/style.css`: desktop/mobile layout and controls.
- `manifest.webmanifest`: PWA metadata and icons.
- `sw.js`: offline cache and fetch handling.
- `android/`: preserved Android TWA bundle configuration and build artifacts.
- `.well-known/assetlinks.json`: Android app association metadata.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `js/game.js`, `js/render.js`, and `js/ui.js` were untracked in the recorded repository status.
- Browser checks used Chromium via a temporary CDP harness in `/tmp/opencode`; the repository server was started with `python3 -m http.server 8123`.
- `android/twa-manifest.json` references a hosted domain and remote icon URLs; confirm these match the final deployment before treating Android packaging as verified.

10: 3. Wait for Gradle sync to complete.

12: 5. Select **Android App Bundle** (.aab) and click Next.
13: 6. Create or select your release keystore.
14: 7. Click **Create** / **Finish**.

## Objective
- Finish and verify the existing browser-playable Vanguard Ballistics game, including its campaign, skirmish mode, and PWA/Android packaging.

## Requirements
- Provide a six-operation campaign and endless skirmish mode.
- Support desktop, mobile, touch, and gamepad layouts.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for visual checks and read only the latest.

## Decisions
- Continue from the existing implementation and validate it in-browser rather than restarting.
- Use synthesized audio and procedural maps; retain Android packaging artifacts under `android/`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game, menus, HUD, campaign, skirmish, PWA manifest, and offline service worker.
- Browser checks covered campaign progression/results, skirmish waves/retry, armory/upgrades, settings, touch controls, gamepad firing, and grenade use; JavaScript syntax checks passed and no runtime errors were observed.
- Saved visual-check JPEGs under `/tmp/opencode/`; latest screenshots are `shot-80-mobile-hud.jpg` through `shot-83-desktop-menu.jpg`.

### Active
- Validate PWA and Android configuration against the completed web app and review remaining control/gameplay flows.
- Review uncommitted changes and summarize verification.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Validate service-worker offline boot and PWA asset cache entries.
2. Resolve Android host, icon URL, and asset association mismatches before claiming TWA packaging is verified.
3. Re-run any remaining gameplay/control checks, inspect the latest screenshots, then review `git status`.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: simulation, combat, mission flow, persistence, and gamepad handling.
- `js/main.js`: application initialization and service-worker registration.
- `js/render.js`: canvas renderer, camera, and visual effects.
- `js/ui.js`: menus, HUD, panels, and results.
- `css/style.css`: desktop/mobile layout and controls.
- `manifest.webmanifest`: PWA metadata and icon paths.
- `sw.js`: offline cache and fetch handling.
- `android/twa-manifest.json`: TWA host and remote icon configuration.
- `android/android-project/app/build.gradle`: Android project host and asset statement.
- `android/well-known/assetlinks.json`: app association metadata.
- `/tmp/opencode/t13.mjs`: latest desktop/mobile and controller browser checks.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `css/style.css` is modified; `js/game.js`, `js/main.js`, `js/render.js`, `js/ui.js`, `manifest.webmanifest`, and `sw.js` are untracked.
- `android/twa-manifest.json` uses the `ais-dev-hcmrpxfxeghhafe2exzkcf-78925681119.us-east1.run.app` host, while `android/android-project/app/build.gradle` uses the `ais-pre-hcmrpxfxeghhafe2exzkcf-78925681119.us-east1.run.app` host; TWA icons also reference remote `pwa-*` paths unlike local `assets/icon-*`. Deployment host and signing fingerprint need confirmation.
